model.rationale: Fundamentals point decisively toward McAdams after redistricting, and markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price his win probability at 94-96%. His overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending advantage over Owen reinforces a Safe D rating despite the absence of polls.
model.watch: Any late polling showing the district's new electorate behaving more like old UT-01, or a surge of Republican outside spending, would warrant moving this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This open seat was redrawn after the 2020 cycle and now sits on strongly Democratic-leaning fundamentals, with the district lean and the national environment both pointing the same direction. Ben McAdams enters as the clear favorite, and prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price his chances in the mid-90s.

The money gap is stark: McAdams has raised over $2.2 million and benefits from roughly $2.7 million in outside support, while Republican Riley Owen has raised about $133,000 with minimal cash on hand. With no independent or third-party polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals and market pricing, both of which point to a comfortable Democratic win.
